payload.body: dc: the README is drafted for your review: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-matts-Devel-prj-Pplr/da774a51-7916-4f68-b76b-37c788cb4a76/scratchpad/docs/README.md, with the diff at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-matts-Devel-prj-Pplr/da774a51-7916-4f68-b76b-37c788cb4a76/scratchpad/docs/README.diff. It is banked on dc/wp13-docs at 88e30c4 and lands after C5 with the CHANGELOG, as you ruled. It describes the tree after the cutover. Installation: Homebrew named as the release path that arrives with 2.0.0, not yet released, with the tap, the targets and the signing as install-release.md settles them. Until then, build from a checkout (the maintainer section). Then PPLR_DATA, doctor and handler --install. New sections: a Configuration table of every setting with its default, read off config.rs; the People tree in ASCII, with the per-person .index for aliases and refreshed; and a commands-at-a-glance table of all 31 commands from pplr help, each also documented below, grouped as People, Meetings and contact, Tags and search, pplr:// links, Apple Contacts, Finder icons and pplr itself. Fixed: the badge (tests.yml); handler --install (registers the app beside pplr; nothing is built into ~/Applications); applyicons (the About and Meetings folders and each meeting); setpicfordir and doctor --fix gain sections; the sidecar is beside pplr and nothing compiles; no uv; the backup default is XDG, with doctor naming the old ~/Library folder; meetings with no date lists today's; the seven facets; the inferred-is-relationship rule; and the divergences where users meet them (contact log's one --email, apply-plan by header names, pull's non-UTF-8 refusal). The examples now use the fixture's vocabulary and people (Blackwood, Esme; Okafor, Chidi; Quennell, Imogen), plus Kemp, Jon and Grifiths, Glen from the bats suite. The About and meeting examples are what pplr new and the template write, in text fences, so that prettier cannot reflow them. Also changed: Requirements (macOS on Apple silicon or Linux; claude, fileicon, Contacts access and Full Disk Access optional; no Python, jq or Swift toolchain at run time), Troubleshooting, Contributing (one Rust crate), the maintainer section (build, check all with nopython, test all, PPLR_UNDER_TEST's dev-build default, people-leak, and the release order as devbin will run it), and the licence, which is now MIT, as LICENSE.md and the formula say. It keeps the title the bats test asserts; help --details prints it verbatim. Prettier passes, it is ASCII only, and people-leak is clean on it, staged in my scratch clone. Two points. (a) doctor still checks for jq, 'the commands not yet ported to Rust need it' (doctor.rs:353). Nothing else in src runs jq, so the row should go with the fallback in WP13. Is it cc's, or mine as WP12's author? The README says no jq is needed. (b) cc tells me its C1 and C4 make CLAUDE.md's two factual edits (the PPLR_UNDER_TEST default, and nopython in check all's list). My CLAUDE.md pointers build on them, beside a pointer for tools/nopython next to people-leak's. ARCHITECTURE.md is next.
